To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fetal and neonatal exposures to losartan were negligible during early gestation and increased during late gestation and lactational exposure, and the relative increased sensitivity to losartan of the fetus, compared to the neonates, is related to the route of exposure and the degree of exposure, which in turn is dependent on the stage of gestation and the ontogeny and expression of the renin-angiotensin system.
the fetal and neonatal rat is highly sensitive to losartan-induced developmental and/or reproductive toxicity.
the fetal and neonatal rat are more sensitive than adult rats to the renal toxicity of losartan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of losartan on the development of the rat kidney and its associated urinary tract.
the effects of angiotensin receptor antagonists on fetal and neonatal development.
the pharmacokinetics of losartan and the ontogeny and function of the renin-angiotensin system during gestation and early postnatal development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fetal exposure to losarten and its active metabolites during the critical developmental period is sufficient for the observed adverse effects on the kidney, but the neonatal exposure is not.
losartan and/or EXP3174 are not detectable in the fetus during the critical developmental period (GD 15-20) when losartan is administered during the first 2 weeks of gestation (GD 6-15).
losartan is a potent AT1 receptor antagonist that can cross the placenta, but not the blood-brain barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
losartan is a safe and effective antihypertensive agent during pregnancy.
losartan and/or EXP3174 are present in the fetus at concentrations that could potentially affect the development of the kidney.
losartan and the metabolite, EXP-3174, are readily detectable in the plasma of the rat fetuses on GD20 and neonates during lactation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relative increased susceptibility of the fetus as opposed to the neonate is dependent on the degree of exposure, which in turn, is dependent on the route of exposure and time of administration.
the fetal exposure to losartans and their active metabolite was much higher than the neonatal exposure during the critical time period.

the relative increased susceptibility of the fetus to losartan-induced nephrotoxicity is related to the time of exposure (GD 15-20) and route of exposure (maternal-fetal transfer) rather than a difference in the pharmacokinetics of losartan or EXP3174 in the fetus and neonate.
